summary.headline: Sula Q4 FY26 revenue rose 7% YoY to INR 142 crore, but gross margin pressure from grape mix kept EBITDA roughly flat in absolute terms.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue returned to growth at 7% YoY to INR 142 crore, driven by a 5% rise in Own Brands and 17% growth in Wine Tourism revenue. Gross profit fell 3% YoY as a shift to wine grapes and higher wine carryover cut gross margin by about 350-400 bps, and the absence of a prior-year INR 3.5 crore Karnataka inventory gain added about 150 bps of pressure. Management cut operating costs 3% YoY, holding EBITDA at similar absolute levels, and PAT fell 34% on a high prior-year tax credit. Full-year FY26 revenue fell 2% to INR 596 crore excluding a prior-year one-off, with Own Brands down 5%.

financial_highlights.metric: Q4 gross margin impact from grape mix and carryover
FY26 EBITDA (excl. prior-year INR 10 crore WIPS gain)

financial_highlights.value: INR 86 crore; around INR 81 crore after April payout of INR 8 crore

segments.name: Own Brands
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 5% YoY, with elite and premium up double digits; FY26 Own Brands fell 5%. The Source grew over 35% in Q4 and over 20% for FY26, reaching over 10% of Own Brands.

segments.name: Wine Tourism
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 17% YoY on 11% higher footfalls; FY26 revenue grew 20%, and total Wine Tourism revenue including wine sales crossed INR 110 crore. Room capacity rose 50% to 154 keys with The Haven; core resort occupancy was over 80% in Q4 and total occupancy over 70%.

segments.name: CSD (institutional/canteen channel)
segments.commentary: FY26 CSD sales grew 21%. Preliminary approval received for five more listings, taking the total from 9 to 14, with completion targeted by year-end and launches by Q4 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Grape mix impact to weigh on profitability for the next couple of quarters, partly offset by lower inventory carrying costs, cost reductions and lower finance costs; management expects grape-mix margin pressure to ease after Q3 FY27.
Management does not expect margins to return to the ~30% operating margin of FY24 soon but is 'quietly optimistic' about YoY margin improvement from Q1 FY27.
Regular capex in FY27 expected below FY26 levels (excluding Chandon); Wine Tourism capex in FY27 to be about 3x winery capex.
Price increases of 2-3% a year planned in free-pricing states including Maharashtra; no hikes planned on wines above INR 1,200 a bottle.
Four newer wines to be scaled up about 40% in FY27; Chandon 19-acre estate acquisition expected to close in H1 FY27.
Target of 80%+ renewable energy share with battery storage; renewable share reached 75% in FY26.
Wine Tourism expected to add 200-300 bps to its share of revenue in FY27 versus FY26 (about 19% in FY26); next resort target of more than 200 keys within about 1.5 years.
capex_capacity: Chandon's 19-acre Dindori estate: binding agreement signed; regulatory approvals and conveyance deed pending; closing expected in H1 FY27.
Third bottle shop at Domaine Dindori (Nashik) targeted to open in Q1 FY27, on the Jaulke Wani highway.
SulaFest amphitheatre capacity expansion to complete in Q2 FY27.
5,000 sq ft air-conditioned event pavilion at Nashik flagship campus expected operational in Q3 FY27.
New tasting room at Domaine Sula (near Bangalore) opened in Q4 FY26.
Production of four recent launches (The Source Moscato, The Source Pinot Noir, Sula Muscat Blanc, Sula Merlot) to be raised about 40% in FY27.
demand_pricing: Management says trade discounting remains unsustainably high industry-wide, while Sula runs much lower discounts and holds a brand premium.
Elite and premium share of Own Brands rose to 79% in Q4 FY26 from 75% in Q3; management said it will not guide for further growth.
Uttar Pradesh grew over 50% in FY26 and nearly 100% in Q4; a new state policy is expected to expand retail licences.
Telangana, UP and Kerala grew robustly in Q4; Maharashtra and Karnataka showed visible improvement, with Karnataka 'looking much better'.
Packaging cost increases expected in FY27 due to West Asia conflict; EU wine duty cuts expected in about a year, with the FTA minimum import price of EUR 2.50 reportedly up about 5% since signing.
Channel inventories fell at end of Q4 after destocking in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: How do channel inventory levels and discounting in the market compare with recent years?
qa_highlights.answer: Channel inventory came down somewhat at end-Q4 after Q3 destocking. Sula runs far lower discounts than domestic peers, while industry discounting is unsustainably high and some producers may fail.

qa_highlights.question: Will Sula import wines and distribute them?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is looking at it but will proceed cautiously, saying Own Brands offer better profitability than imports and that importing has low barriers to entry and is hard.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be more acquisitions in Wine Tourism?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says it is always open to opportunities and keeps looking, but the Chandon deal needs further investment and no others are yet agreed.

qa_highlights.question: What are the cost pressures and margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: COGS rose in Q4 on grape mix, which will persist for a couple of quarters until the next harvest. Overhead reductions are expected to offset part of this at EBITDA level.

qa_highlights.question: What is the resort plan for FY27 and the elite/premium strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: No specific resort launch announced; a plan to be disclosed by next call. Elite and premium share reached 79% in Q4, and management is not guiding for further gains.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins return to 30%, and what is the FY27 top-line outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not guide to a return to 30% margins soon, expects moderation, and sees growth as the driver of any margin expansion. It is cautiously optimistic about YoY margin improvement.

qa_highlights.question: Can receivables be monetised, and are there plans for other liquor categories or a Chandon resort?
qa_highlights.answer: Telangana corporation payments have resumed after the new excise policy, and receivables are seen as under control. Management is focused on Wine Tourism; no non-wine spirits deal has been found, and the Chandon resort timing and room count were not given.

qa_highlights.question: Where does Wine Tourism's revenue mix and key target stand?
qa_highlights.answer: Wine Tourism is about 19% of FY26 revenue and may rise 200-300 bps in FY27. Keys are to grow in high double digits over two years, with a next project above 200 keys in about 1.5 years.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from the wine-grape mix and bulk wine carryover will persist until the next harvest, with relief expected after Q3 FY27.
Packaging cost inflation from the West Asia conflict and rising fuel and power costs may pressure FY27 margins.
Industry discounting and competitive pricing in popular and economy segments could limit pricing power.
Pending regulatory approvals and conveyance deed for the Chandon acquisition; the Chandon resort timeline and room count were not disclosed.
Customs and EU duty changes could bring cheaper European imports into the premium segment in about a year.
Heat-related storage and retail cooling challenges in trade channels, with state corporations not yet providing air-conditioned space for wine in Telangana.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand recovery and Wine Tourism, but cautious on margins, which management expects to stay under pressure for a couple of quarters. Management was evasive on specifics such as the next resort's location, margin targets and any non-wine spirits deal.
key_quotes: After a challenging few quarters we delivered a marked improvement in Q4, returning to growth with revenue up 7% year -on-year.
The Source sales grew by over 35% in Q4 and over 20% for the full year FY '26
So, this would be reflected in lower inventory of bulk wine moving forward, which, of course, has a great positive impact on cash flows and therefore, overall debt.
In terms of margins, I would not guide that we are going to return to 30% anytime soon.
